---
title: "Troubleshooting"
---

## "The process cannot access the file"

DuckDB allows one process to open a database at a time. A running `skemman` command locks
everyone else out, including your IDE's database panel and any R or Python session.

Close the other connection. Note that closing an editor tab does not disconnect an IDE
data source — disconnect it explicitly, or quit the IDE.

After any write, run `CHECKPOINT;` so the `.wal` file folds back into the database.

## The progress bar moves but nothing is written

Look at `failed` in the progress bar and then at `logs/titlepage.log`. Each line names the
thesis, its handle URL, whether the failure is permanent, and why.

Common reasons:

| Reason | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `not a PDF (restricted or a landing page)` | The server answered with something other than a PDF. Permanent. |
| `download failed: HTTPError 404` | The bitstream is gone. Permanent. |
| `unreadable PDF: PdfStreamError` | The file arrived truncated. Retried next run. |

## "Stream has ended unexpectedly"

The PDF arrived incomplete. Skemman serves very large files unreliably, and does not
always send `Content-Length`, so a short read cannot always be detected during download.

Large files are fetched last, so this affects the tail of a run. `--max-mb` skips them
altogether:

```bash
skemman titlepage-load --max-mb 50
```

## Encrypted PDFs

Some are AES-encrypted without a password. `pypdf` needs `cryptography` for those; it is a
declared dependency, so a normal install handles it.

## Nothing happens

If every thesis already has a row, there is nothing to do. To re-parse from cache without
fetching:

```bash
duckdb thesis.db -c "drop table thesis_titlepage"
skemman titlepage-load
```

## Font and xref warnings

`pypdf` logs a great deal about unusual fonts and cross-reference tables. These are
suppressed below the error level, because the text extracts regardless. If you want them,
raise the level for the `pypdf` logger.
